Agreement to run a controlled traffic ramp once VPC/network rules are in place; Redwood to deliver SOC2 and batching tuning suggestions. Customer to provide network window and KMS info.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-06 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (SE), Marco (CSM), Lina (Solutions), Maya (CTO), Alex (Platform), Samir (Security), Tara (PM)

[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. quick agenda — gate review for the early adopter pilot, a quick look at the benchmark anomalies we saw yesterday, and confirm timelines for the traffic ramp.

[00:27] Maya: Yeah thanks, Evan. we got some folks pulled in. main thing for us is visibility on the network plan and the security checkboxes. we can't move to staged traffic without a KMS pattern approved.

[00:45] Priya: totally, Maya. on the KMS front, Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. typically we ask for a test key with limited scope first, then we swap to production key during cutover. Samir, did you want to add anything?

[01:05] Samir: yeah, just to reiterate, we need an audit trail and we want to see access logs forwarded to our SIEM. also need the key rotation policy. trying to avoid any surprises during SOC review.

[01:25] Alex: quick infra question — firewall rules. do you have static egress IPs for the hosted endpoints or is it per-region and dynamic?

[01:40] Evan: good question. for the hosted API we publish a stable range of egress IPs per region; I'll attach the CIDR list after the call. for Dedicated or Private we can avoid egress entirely with VPC peering.

[01:58] Alex: ok that works. we'll open a ticket with cloud infra and target next week for the window.

[02:12] Tara: on timeline — our target is to start a limited ramp next Tuesday, but that's contingent on the VPC peering and keys.

[02:28] Priya: about the benchmark anomalies — yesterday's run showed an unexpected tail latency around the 99.9th percentile on long-context requests (2k tokens). average p50/p95 looked fine, but spikes hit 1.2s extra at certain times.

[02:52] Maya: we saw that in our logs too. looked like it coincided with a burst of small requests from another test team, maybe contention?

[03:08] Priya: possible. couple things to call out: our SDK does continuous batching by default but we've got knobs — batch size, max wait, and prefix caching. with long context you can also get backpressure on KV cache. We suggested lowering max_wait to 15ms and increasing batch size to allow better packing for those tails, but that trades a few ms average.

[03:32] Marco: can you send an example config? want to make sure our ops team can apply it without disrupting other stages.

[03:45] Priya: yep, I'll share a sample YAML with ranges and safe defaults. Lina will add notes for rollback.

[04:00] Lina: and we'll annotate which metrics to watch so you can auto-rollback if p95 jumps.

[04:12] Alex: curious — would switching to Redwood Dedicated for the pilot reduce these spikes? how big is the delta?

[04:26] Evan: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and stricter isolation so you'll see more consistent tails; typically tail latency improvement depends on workload — for throughput-heavy long-context runs it can help a lot. but Dedicated is a procurement shift and longer lead time.

[04:45] Maya: procurement might be okay later, but for now we want to validate the hosted path if possible. saves us a bunch of overhead.

[05:00] Priya: another interim approach: pin to a verified model variant with smaller kv footprint for prefix-heavy queries; that often reduces the cache churn. we'll propose a model profile in the doc.

[05:18] Samir: on compliance — can Redwood stream audit logs to our log sink?

[05:28] Evan: yes, we can forward via a secure syslog or S3 push with encryption in transit. we'll need the endpoint and auth method.

[05:40] Samir: ok, we'll draft the sink and owners.

[06:02] Tara: detail on the traffic ramp — we plan to start with synthetic traffic for 24 hours at ~10 RPS then step to 50 RPS. does Redwood have a recommended synthetic profile?

[06:20] Priya: we can provide a synthetic script that emulates your mix — 60% short requests, 40% long-context. we'll also instrument it to highlight KV cache miss rate and batching efficiency.

[06:38] Alex: can we run it through our staging VPC first so we capture egress behavior?

[06:48] Evan: yes, if you set up VPC peering or provide the test subnet we'll run the traffic there. note — peering requires a maintenance window for routing changes.

[07:05] Maya: what's the typical time to establish peering?

[07:12] Evan: usually 24-48 hours for the ticket to be processed by cloud infra, plus <1 hour to test once we have subnets. we'll push the egress CIDRs now so you can start the request.

[07:28] Priya: I want to call out one anomaly from yesterday: a single hot request pattern caused cache eviction; it was a few large doc-indexing calls at once. If you can avoid synchronized large batches during the ramp that would help.

[07:48] Alex: noted — we'll stagger the indexing and pre-warm the cache.

[08:02] Samir: encryption-in-use question — do you support in-flight encryption for the KV cache?

[08:12] Priya: yes, TLS in transit. at rest depends on deployment — hosted uses our managed encryption, private allows customer-managed keys.

[08:26] Evan: also to be transparent, our default logs redact PII but you can opt for increased verbosity with a secure transfer.

[08:38] Tara: please add that to the security doc.

[08:45] Evan: will do. Marco, are we tracking the open security checklist items?

[08:52] Marco: I have a running board in the pilot tracker; I'll drop a link after this call. current open items: SOC2 doc, network CIDRs, KMS owners, SSO/SAML integration plan.

[09:10] Maya: SSO — we want SAML right away. can we stage with a test IdP?

[09:20] Evan: yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO; we can onboard a test IdP for staging. we will send SAML metadata and a guide.

[09:30] Priya: back to perf — one more suggestion: enable prefix/KV caching on your common prompts — even a small hit there reduces token cost and tail.

[09:45] Alex: how invasive is that change to our codebase?

[09:52] Priya: it's a thin SDK change; we provide wrappers. should be a matter of toggling and adding a cache key generator — I'll share code samples.

[10:10] Maya: ok. good. any updates on cost modeling? we need to understand the delta if we increase batch size (i.e., small latency trade for lower token price).

[10:22] Evan: we'll produce a simple cost scenario spreadsheet — p50/p95 vs batch config and token utilization so you can evaluate.

[10:30] Tara: please include a line for Dedicated vs Hosted cost baseline.

[10:36] Evan: yes.

[10:45] Priya: last operational note — we'll recommend a canary policy: route 5% of traffic for 2 hours, measure, then 20% for 6 hours before full ramp.

[10:58] Alex: that timeline works for us.

[11:06] Evan: summary / next steps: I'll send SOC2 and the egress CIDRs today; Priya will share batching-yaml and sample scripts; Alex will open firewall ticket and provide subnets; Samir will outline KMS requirements and owners. We agreed to aim for synthetic 24h ramp starting 2026-08-12 pending network window.

[11:30] Maya: sounds good. one more ask — can we get a short runbook for emergency rollback if latency exceeds threshold?

[11:40] Priya: yes, we'll prepare a runbook with immediate steps and automated rollback flags.

[11:52] Evan: thanks all. Marco will follow up with the pilot tracker link and I'll put the action items into CRM. meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
